finding.claim: validate uses `!== undefined || !== null` which is always true, so it always reports "id is required" and "value is required" even for complete payloads.
finding.title: validation condition always true

verifier.reason: The conditions at src/validation.ts:8 and src/validation.ts:11 use `!== undefined || !== null`, which is tautologically true since a value cannot be both undefined and null, so both errors are always pushed even for complete payloads.

finding.claim: collect uses forEach with an async callback and returns immediately, so results is always empty and async errors are never caught.
finding.title: async forEach never awaited

verifier.reason: The code at src/analytics.ts:6 uses tasks.forEach with an async callback whose awaited pushes at src/analytics.ts:7 are not awaited by collect, which returns results immediately at src/analytics.ts:12, and the surrounding try/catch at src/analytics.ts:5 cannot catch the discarded async callback rejections.

finding.claim: buildSummary appends to module-level totals then sums totals, so repeated calls double-count prior entries.
finding.title: module accumulator double-counts

verifier.reason: Confirmed: buildSummary at src/ledger.ts:12-15 calls post(entries) which pushes onto the module-level totals at src/ledger.ts:6-9, then sums all of totals without resetting, so a second call re-includes entries from the first call.

finding.claim: rotateToken does not await store.save before store.get, so the read can return the stale token.
finding.title: missing await on save before read

verifier.reason: At src/session.ts:11 store.save(userId, token) is called without await despite SessionStore.save returning Promise<void> at src/session.ts:2, and src/session.ts:12 immediately returns store.get(userId), so the read can race the pending save and return the stale token.

finding.claim: start overwrites this.timer with a new setInterval without clearing the existing interval, leaking the prior timer.
finding.title: timer handle replaced without clear

verifier.reason: The start method at src/scheduler.ts:7-11 unconditionally assigns this.timer = setInterval(...) with no clearInterval call or null guard, and no stop method exists in src/scheduler.ts:3-20, so a second call loses the prior timer handle.

finding.claim: pageSlice uses slice(start, end + 1) where end is start+size, returning size+1 elements instead of size.
finding.title: page slice off-by-one

verifier.reason: Confirmed at src/paging.ts:9-10: end is start+size and slice(start, end+1) is end-exclusive, so it returns up to size+1 elements instead of size.

finding.claim: sortScores uses default Array.sort without numeric comparator, sorting numbers lexicographically and breaking topScore.
finding.title: numeric sort uses lexicographic order

verifier.reason: The code at src/scores.ts:2 uses scores.slice().sort() with no comparator, so JavaScript sorts numbers as strings, and topScore at src/scores.ts:5-7 returns the last element, which will not be the numeric maximum for multi-digit values.

finding.claim: withinQuota uses `< max` while the contract states max is inclusive, rejecting requests that exactly fill quota.
finding.title: inclusive quota uses strict less-than

verifier.reason: The contract at src/quota.ts:2 states max is inclusive, but src/quota.ts:6 returns used + amount < max, so an exact-fill request returns false.

finding.claim: normalizeSettings uses `||` for defaults, so legitimate 0 values for pageSize/budgetCents are replaced with defaults.

evidence.snippet: // Optional values are read from settings where 0 is a legitimate value.

finding.title: falsy default replaces legitimate zero

verifier.reason: The code at src/settings.ts:13-14 uses `raw.pageSize || 20` and `raw.budgetCents || 1000`, so a legitimate 0 is falsy and is replaced by the default, consistent with the note at src/settings.ts:18 that 0 is a legitimate value.
